mainTopic: The inner-altar sprinklings of יום כיפור, the meaning of 'טהרו של מזבח', where the leftover blood is poured, and whether there is מעילה in it.
overview: This עמוד finishes explaining how the כהן גדול sprinkled blood on the inner altar on יום כיפור, and then follows the משנה line by line. First the גמרא tries several ways to explain the מחלוקת between רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי. It settles on the view that they argue about whether the הקפה was done by hand or by foot. A ברייתא about two כהנים גדולים from the first בית המקדש shows this was a real disagreement, and each one had a reason. Next, the גמרא shows that רבי אליעזר's view in the משנה follows רבי יהודה's report of it. It then explains that 'טהרו של מזבח' means the cleared top of the altar. Everyone agrees the seven sprinklings go where the corner placements ended; חנניא and רבי יוסי only argue about where the entrance was. Then the גמרא explains where the leftover blood is poured: always at the base closest to the כהן. There are other views from רבי ישמעאל and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי. The עמוד ends with a ברייתא arguing whether using that leftover blood counts as מעילה.

steps.title: New explanation: the dispute is about going around by hand or by foot
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees we learn the inner altar from the outer altar if the כהן walks around it. The real argument is whether he walks around (הקפה ברגל) or stands still and reaches around (הקפה ביד).
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say this instead: if we hold the going-around is done by walking, then everyone agrees that we learn the inside altar from the outside altar. Here they argue about something else. One master holds the going-around is done by hand, and the other master holds it is done by foot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way to explain the מחלוקת between רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי. It no longer says they argue about learning פנים מחוץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the outer altar the כהן walked around, starting at the southeast corner. If he also walks around the inner altar, everyone would copy that order. רבי עקיבא holds he stood in place and sprinkled by reaching (ביד), so the outer-altar order does not apply and he starts at the corner closest to him. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds he walked (ברגל), so he copies the outer altar.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say instead (introduces another possible explanation)
Going around the altar while sprinkling
By foot, meaning actually walking around
By hand, meaning standing still and reaching around
We learn the inner altar's procedure from the outer altar's

steps.confusionAlert: Note that 'הקפה ביד' is still called a הקפה, a going-around. It is just done by reaching instead of walking. Do not think one side says there is no going-around at all.

steps.terutzMaskana: They agree on the comparison. They argue over whether the הקפה is by hand or by foot.

steps.title: Another explanation: do we learn going around by hand from going around by foot
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees the inner altar's הקפה is by hand. The argument is whether a hand-going-around copies the rules of a foot-going-around.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say this instead: everyone agrees the going-around is by hand. Here they argue about this. One master holds we learn hand from foot, and the other master holds we do not learn it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second new explanation. This time both sides agree the כהן reached around by hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רבי יוסי הגלילי says that even reaching by hand should follow the walking order of the outer altar, starting at the southeast. רבי עקיבא says reaching by hand is different from walking, so we do not copy the outer altar's order.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
everyone agrees the encircling is by hand,
and here they disagree about this:
one master holds we learn hand from foot,
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי הגלילי

phrases.english: and one master holds: we do not learn it.
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא הַקָּפָה בַּיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative. In Step 1 the sides argued about hand versus foot. Here both agree on hand, and they argue about the comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the dispute to a different underlying question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: They argue whether the הקפה is by hand or by foot.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree it is by hand. They argue whether יד is learned from רגל.

steps.title: Challenge: the end of the משנה shows the first opinion holds the כהן walked
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's view that the כהן 'stood in his place' is presented as a separate opinion. That implies the תנא קמא did not hold this. So רבי יוסי הגלילי cannot hold הקפה ביד.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does רבי יוסי הגלילי really hold the going-around is by hand? The end of the משנה teaches that רבי אליעזר says he stood in his place and sprinkled. That implies the first teacher does not hold this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation in Step 2 using the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Standing in place and sprinkling' is the same as הקפה ביד. רבי אליעזר says this as his own separate opinion, so the earlier view must disagree and hold the כהן walked. That contradicts Step 2, which had רבי יוסי הגלילי agreeing it was by hand.

keyTerms.meaning: The end clause of the משנה
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הַקָּפָה בַּיָּד?
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei HaGelili hold the encircling is by hand?
But from the fact that the latter clause teaches:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
he stood in his place and sprinkled,

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא לָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: it follows that the first tanna does not hold so.
phrases.notes: Here the תנא קמא is understood as רבי יוסי הגלילי

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הַקָּפָה בַּיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in Step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 2's claim that everyone, including רבי יוסי הגלילי, holds הקפה ביד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's 'standing in place' view is listed separately, which shows the תנא קמא held the כהן walked (ברגל).

steps.title: Conclusion: return to the hand-versus-foot explanation
steps.stepSummary: The second explanation is rejected. The גמרא confirms the first one: the dispute is whether the הקפה is by hand or by foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear the way we answered at first: one master holds the going-around is by hand, and the other master holds it is by foot.
steps.whatsHappening: Since Step 2 fell apart, the גמרא goes back and settles on the explanation from Step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 fits the wording of the משנה. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds the כהן walked, which is exactly what the inference from רבי אליעזר required. רבי עקיבא holds by hand, so he does not follow the outer altar's starting corner.
steps.whatToRemember: The accepted explanation of the מחלוקת: רבי עקיבא holds הקפה ביד and רבי יוסי הגלילי holds הקפה ברגל. Everyone agrees that if the כהן walks, we copy the outer altar (פנים מחוץ).

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear as we answered originally:
one master holds the encircling is by hand,
and one master holds the encircling is by foot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge in Step 3 and returns to the explanation in Step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute is about הקפה ביד versus הקפה ברגל.

steps.title: Final explanation: is the inner altar's edge like the outer altar's, or like one corner of it
steps.stepSummary: The disagreement may be about whether the edge of the small inner altar counts like the edge of the outer altar. The other view treats the whole inner altar as the size of just one corner of the outer altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say they argue about this. One master holds the edge around the inner altar is like the edge around the outer altar. The other master holds the whole inner altar stands in place of just one corner of the outer altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more possible way to explain the מחלוקת. This one is based on how we compare the two altars' shapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner altar was only one אמה by one אמה, about the size of a single corner of the large outer altar. If its edge counts like the outer altar's edge, the outer altar's going-around rules apply. If the whole altar counts as just 'one corner,' those rules do not carry over at all. The גמרא itself does not name the sides; it only says 'one master' and 'the other master.' Step 7 shows that the comparison view goes with walking around, and the 'one corner' view goes with reaching by hand.

keyTerms.meaning: The edge or perimeter around the altar
The inner (golden) altar, inside the היכל
The outer altar, in the courtyard

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא, בְּהָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי:
phrases.english: And if you wish, say they disagree about this:
one master holds: the perimeter of the inner altar
is like the perimeter of the outer altar,

steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the dispute to a different underlying question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute is about hand versus foot.
steps.terutzMaskana: Alternatively, the dispute is whether the inner altar's perimeter compares to the outer altar's perimeter or to just one of its corners.

steps.title: Two High Priests remembered the service differently
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל shows that the hand-versus-foot question was a real disagreement. Two כהנים גדולים from the first בית המקדש remembered doing it differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי ישמעאל said that two כהנים גדולים were still alive from the first בית המקדש. One said, 'I went around by hand.' The other said, 'I went around by foot.' Each one had a reason for what he said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the 'by hand or by foot' question really was argued about, even among actual כהנים גדולים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 concluded that the dispute is whether the הקפה is ביד or ברגל. This ברייתא backs that up with real people who actually did the service in two different ways. Each one had a reason, and the next step shows that these reasons are exactly the two views given in Step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: gives a reason for his words

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yishmael said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי כֹהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים נִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ בְּמִקְדָּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: Two High Priests remained from the First Temple.
This one says: I went around by hand,
phrases.notes: He stood still and reached around the altar.

phrases.english: and that one says: I went around by foot.
phrases.notes: He walked around the altar.

phrases.english: This one gave a reason for his words,
and that one gave a reason for his words.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: שְׁנֵי כֹהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים נִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ בְּמִקְדָּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא confirming that the hand-versus-foot disagreement really existed.
steps.raayaObject: The hand-versus-foot dispute (Step 4) was a real one, and the reasons behind it are the ones given in Step 5: whether the inner altar's perimeter is like the outer altar's, or whether the whole inner altar counts as one corner.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל about two כהנים גדולים of the first בית המקדש.

steps.title: The reasons of the two High Priests
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out each כהן גדול's reason. One compares the inner altar's edge to the outer altar's edge. The other says the whole inner altar is only the size of one corner of the outer altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who walked around reasoned that 'around' the inner altar means the same as 'around' the outer altar, which is done by walking. The one who reached around reasoned that the whole inner altar is only as big as one corner of the outer altar, and a single corner is done by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each כהן גדול's way of doing the service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'by foot' כהן treats the word סביב the same way for both altars, so walking is required. The 'by hand' כהן says the inner altar is so small that it is like a single corner of the outer altar. A single corner never needs walking. These two reasons match exactly the idea raised in Step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: around (the word in the פסוק that requires going around)
stands / takes up the space of

steps.whatToRemember: Hand or foot depends on one question. Is the inner altar treated like the big outer altar, so you walk around it? Or is it treated like one small corner of it, so you reach by hand?

phrases.english: This one gave a reason for his words:
phrases.notes: This is the one who walked around.

phrases.english: 'Around' of the inner altar
is like 'around' of the outer altar,

phrases.english: and that one gave a reason for his words:

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה נוֹתֵן טַעַם לִדְבָרָיו: סָבִיב דְּמִזְבֵּחַ פְּנִימִי כְּסָבִיב דְּמִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Walking is based on comparing the two altars. Reaching by hand is based on treating the whole inner altar as one corner of the outer altar.

steps.title: Which version of רבי אליעזר does the משנה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's view in the משנה, that the כהן stood in one place. Then it asks whose version of his view the משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי אליעזר says, he stood in his place and sprinkled. Whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, quoting רבי אליעזר. It sets up a question: which תנא's report of רבי אליעזר's view does our משנה match?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Later תנאים reported רבי אליעזר's view in different ways. The משנה also describes which direction the blood was put on each corner. So the גמרא wants to know whose report the משנה follows. This step only asks the question; the answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: sprinkles the blood (literally: purifies the altar)

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: He would stand in his place and sprinkle.
Our משנה, whose view is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the view of רבי אליעזר in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's version of רבי אליעזר's view matches the wording of our משנה.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה follows רבי יהודה's report of רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question in a short line: the משנה follows רבי יהודה. The proof comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were two different reports of what רבי אליעזר held, one from רבי מאיר and one from רבי יהודה. The details in our משנה match רבי יהודה's report.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהודה's version of רבי אליעזר's view.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's report: downward on all corners except the diagonal one
steps.stepSummary: The proof ברייתא begins with רבי מאיר's version. The כהן stood in one place and put the blood from top to bottom on every corner, except the corner diagonally across from him, which he did from bottom to top.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי מאיר says that רבי אליעזר says the כהן stands in his place and sprinkles. On all the corners he put the blood from above downward, except the corner on the diagonal, which he did from below upward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that proves its answer. First it gives רבי מאיר's report of רבי אליעזר, which is not the version our משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי מאיר's version, the normal direction is downward. This way the blood does not run up his sleeve. The far, diagonal corner is too hard to reach from above, so there he goes upward. This is the opposite of our משנה, so the משנה cannot be רבי מאיר.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate disputes on this דף. Do not mix them up. The hand-versus-foot dispute is one thing. Here, everyone in the ברייתא agrees that רבי אליעזר said the כהן stood still. The only argument is about the direction (up or down) of the blood on each corner.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Meir says:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
He stands in his place and sprinkles,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל כּוּלָּן הָיָה נוֹתֵן מִמַּעְלָה לְמַטָּה,
phrases.english: and on all of them he would put the blood from above downward,
phrases.notes: This keeps the blood from running down into his sleeve.

phrases.english: except for that corner on the diagonal,
which he puts from below upward.
phrases.notes: It is too far to reach comfortably from above.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the ברייתא that proves the answer of Step 9, starting with the version the משנה does not follow.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, not רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording two reports of רבי אליעזר's view.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's report: upward on all corners except the one right in front
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reports the opposite. The כהן put the blood from bottom to top on every corner, except the corner right in front of him, which he did from top to bottom so his clothes would not get dirty. This matches our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says that רבי אליעזר says the כהן stands in his place and sprinkles. On all the corners he puts the blood from below upward, except the one directly in front of him, which he does from above downward, so that his garments do not get dirty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא with רבי יהודה's version. This is the one that matches our משנה, which proves the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, upward is the normal and easier direction. The only exception is the nearest corner. Going upward there could splash blood onto his בגדי כהונה, and soiled garments are not allowed for the service. Our משנה says exactly this, so it follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה follows רבי יהודה's report of רבי אליעזר. The כהן stands still and puts the blood upward on every corner, except the one right in front of him, which he does downward to protect his clothes.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a single תנא's view (רבי אליעזר) can come down to us in two versions. The גמרא matches the wording of the משנה to the correct version.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Rabbi Eliezer says:
He stands in his place and sprinkles,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל כּוּלָּן הוּא נוֹתֵן מִלְּמַטָּה לְמַעְלָה,
phrases.english: and on all of them he puts the blood from below upward,
except for this one that was directly in front of him,
which he puts from above downward,
so that his garments should not get dirty.
phrases.notes: Soiled בגדי כהונה may not be worn for the service.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: בִּמְקוֹמוֹ עוֹמֵד וּמְחַטֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא with the version that matches the משנה, proving Step 9.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's report of רבי אליעזר in the ברייתא, which matches the משנה's wording.

steps.title: What does 'טהרו' of the altar mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase 'he sprinkled on טהרו of the altar' and asks what 'טהרו' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He sprinkled from it on the טהרו of the altar.' What does 'טהרו' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה and asks about one unclear word: 'טהרו'. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the כהן put blood on the four corners of the inner altar. After that he sprinkles seven more times on 'טהרו' of the altar. The word could mean 'its purity' or something else, so the גמרא needs to know exactly where these sprinklings went.

keyTerms.meaning: A hard word in the משנה. It is the place of the seven sprinklings.
The altar. Here it means the inner golden altar.

phrases.aramaic: הִזָּה מִמֶּנּוּ עַל טׇהֳרוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.english: He sprinkled from it on the 'tohoro' of the altar.
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה. 'From it' means from the mixed blood.

phrases.english: What is 'tohoro'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the corner placements (steps 8-11) to the next action in the משנה, the seven sprinklings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word 'טהרו', and so the exact location of the seven sprinklings.

steps.title: First answer: 'טהרו' means the middle of the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא says 'טהרו' means half, the middle, of the altar. He proves it from a common saying about noon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב שילא said: it means the middle of the altar. People say, 'the noon light shines, and it is the middle of the day.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב שילא gives a first explanation. 'טהרו' means the midpoint of the altar, so the כהן sprinkled on the middle of the altar's wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He proves the meaning from everyday speech. 'טיהרא' is noon, the middle of the day. So 'טהרו של מזבח' would be the middle of the altar.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of it, the middle of it
As people say. This brings proof from common speech.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Sheila said:
Half of the altar,
phrases.notes: The midpoint of the altar's side.

phrases.english: as people say:
'The noon light shines, and it is the middle of the day.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'טהרו' means the middle of the altar, like 'טיהרא', the middle of the day.

steps.title: Challenge: the sprinkling was on top of the altar
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the כהן pushed aside the coals and ashes and sprinkled. That means he sprinkled on the top of the altar, not on the middle of its side.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא challenges from a ברייתא: When he sprinkles, he does not sprinkle on the ashes or on the coals. Instead he pushes the coals to this side and that side, and then he sprinkles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה בר רב שילא's answer with a ברייתא. The ברייתא shows the seven sprinklings were on the top surface of the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Coals and ashes sit only on the top of the altar. If the כהן had to clear them away before sprinkling, he was sprinkling on the top. That does not fit 'the middle of the altar's side.'

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
When he sprinkles, he does not sprinkle
not on top of the ash
and not on top of the coals,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא חוֹתֶה גֶּחָלִים אֵילָךְ וְאֵילָךְ, וּמַזֶּה.
phrases.english: rather, he rakes the coals to this side and that side, and sprinkles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב שילא's claim that 'טהרו' is the middle of the altar's side
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Clearing away coals only makes sense on the top surface, so the sprinkling was on top, not on the side.

steps.title: New answer: 'טהרו' means the cleared surface of the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא changes his answer. 'טהרו' means the exposed, cleared part of the altar's top. He proves it from a פסוק where 'טוהר' means clear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Instead, רבה בר רב שילא said: it means the exposed part of the altar. As the פסוק says: 'And like the very sky for clearness.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב שילא drops his first answer and gives a new one. 'טהרו' means the spot on the top of the altar that was cleared of coals so it was bare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' (rather) shows he is taking back his first answer. In the פסוק, 'טוהר' means clearness, like a clear sky. So 'טהרו של מזבח' is the cleared, uncovered surface, which fits the ברייתא exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Here it marks taking back the first answer.

steps.confusionAlert: 'טהרו' here does not mean 'purity' in the sense of טומאה and טהרה. It means 'clear' or 'bare', the place where the coals were pushed aside.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rabba bar Rav Sheila said:
on the exposed part of the altar,
as it is written:
'And like the very heaven for clearness.'
phrases.notes: שמות 24:10

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14 by replacing the explanation in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction and a new definition of the word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'טהרו' means the middle of the altar's side.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'טהרו' means the cleared, exposed surface on top of the altar.
steps.whatToRemember: 'טהרו של מזבח' is the bare spot on top of the inner altar, cleared of coals. That is where the seven sprinklings go.

steps.title: Dispute: north side or south side?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings a dispute. חנניא says the כהן does the sprinklings on the north side of the altar. רבי יוסי says the south side.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: חנניא says, he places it on the north side. רבי יוסי says, he places it on the south side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about where on the altar's top the seven sprinklings are done. Two תנאים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know the sprinklings are on the top. This ברייתא asks which side of the top. חנניא says north and רבי יוסי says south.

phrases.english: It was taught: Chananya says:
He places it on the north side,
Rabbi Yosei says:
He places it on the south side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 15. Now that we know the sprinklings are on top, it asks where on the top.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנניא: the seven sprinklings are on the north side. רבי יוסי: on the south side.

steps.title: What is the root of their dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle חנניא and רבי יוסי disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the dispute. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants the underlying issue, not just the two opinions. It assumes the dispute comes from a deeper difference in how they picture the scene.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the dispute in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides חנניא and רבי יוסי

steps.title: They disagree about where the entrance was
steps.stepSummary: One holds the entrance was in the south. The other holds it was in the north. This changes the כהן's route around the altar, and so where he ends up.
steps.simpleTranslation: One חכם (חנניא) holds the entrance stood in the south. The other חכם (רבי יוסי) holds the entrance stood in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the argument is about a fact: on which side the entrance was. Each one's view of the entrance leads to his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where the כהן enters decides which corner he starts with and which corner he finishes with. Where he finishes decides where he sprinkles on top, as the next step explains. So חנניא, with the entrance in the south, ends up on the north side, and רבי יוסי, with the entrance in the north, ends up on the south side.

phrases.english: One master holds:
phrases.notes: חנניא

phrases.english: The entrance stood in the south,
and one master holds:
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי

phrases.english: The entrance stood in the north.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about where the entrance stood: south (חנניא) or north (רבי יוסי).

steps.title: Shared rule: sprinkle on top where the corners ended
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that the כהן sprinkles on the top of the altar at the place where he finished the corner placements.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees, at least, that where he finishes the corner placements, there he puts the blood on its top.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule that both חנניא and רבי יוסי accept. This shared rule is why their dispute about the entrance changes the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on the rule: the seven top sprinklings are done at the spot where the last corner placement was. They argue only about where that last corner is, because they picture the entrance in different places.

keyTerms.meaning: The placements of blood on the corners

phrases.english: According to everyone, in any case,
where the corner placements are finished,
there he places it on its top.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the entrance dispute in step 18 leads to the north/south rulings in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The top sprinklings are done at the spot where the corner placements end.

steps.title: Why must the top sprinklings follow the last corner?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the agreed rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why everyone agrees to this rule. This sets up the proof from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule that everyone accepts still needs a source. The גמרא now looks for it.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for sprinkling on top at the spot where the corners ended

steps.title: Source: 'וטהרו וקדשו'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'וטהרו וקדשו' teaches that the place where he 'sanctified' the altar (the corners) is the place where he 'purifies' it (the top sprinklings).
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And he shall purify it and sanctify it.' The place where he sanctified it, there he purifies it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from the יום כיפור service. The two words are linked, so the two actions must happen at the same spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וקדשו' refers to the corner placements, and 'וטהרו' refers to the seven sprinklings on 'טהרו של מזבח'. Putting them together in one פסוק teaches that the purifying sprinklings are done where the sanctifying corners ended. This closes the סוגיא: the north/south dispute is only about where the corners end.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees: the seven sprinklings on the top go where the corner placements ended ('מקום שקדשו שם טיהרו'). חנניא and רבי יוסי argue only about where that is, because they disagree about where the entrance was.

phrases.english: The verse says:
'And he shall purify it and sanctify it':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:19

phrases.english: the place where he sanctified it, there he purifies it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 and gives the source for step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'וטהרו וקדשו': where he sanctified (the last corner), there he purifies (the top sprinklings).
steps.whyThisMatters: This links the corner placements and the top sprinklings into one continuous act at one spot. That is why the side of the entrance decides the הלכה.

steps.title: The משנה's rule: leftover inner blood goes on the western base
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the כהן גדול poured the leftover blood on the western יסוד of the outer altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: The leftover blood he would pour on the western base of the outer altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה so it can explain it. The line says where the leftover blood of the יום הכפורים offerings is poured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After all the sprinklings inside are done, some blood is left in the bowl. The משנה says it is poured on the western יסוד (the base) of the outer altar. The next step will give the source for choosing the west side.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover blood that remains after the required sprinklings
The base: a ledge at the bottom of the altar
The outer altar, which stands in the courtyard (the copper altar)

steps.confusionAlert: The blood came from offerings sprinkled inside, but the leftover is poured on the OUTER altar, not the golden altar inside.

phrases.english: The leftover blood he would pour
on the western base
of the outer altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁיָרֵי הַדָּם הָיָה שׁוֹפֵךְ עַל יְסוֹד מַעֲרָבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the sprinklings on top of the altar to the next line of the משנה, about the leftover blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover blood from the inner offerings is poured on the western יסוד of the outer altar.

steps.title: Why the west: it is the first side he reaches
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says to pour the blood at the altar's base. Since the כהן exits the היכל toward the altar's western side, that is the base he reaches first.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the verse says: 'And all the blood of the bull he shall pour out' at the base of the altar. When he goes out from the היכל, he reaches that western side first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source and the reason for the western side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (ויקרא ד:ז) requires pouring at the base of the outer altar, but it does not say which side. The היכל is to the west of the altar. So a כהן walking out of the היכל meets the western side first, and that is where he pours.

phrases.english: As the verse says:
'And all the blood of the bull he shall pour out,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ד:ז. The verse continues: 'at the base of the altar of burnt-offering.'

phrases.english: and when he goes out (of the היכל),
that (western side) is the one he reaches first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source and the reason for the משנה's rule in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the leftover inner blood is poured on the western יסוד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'ואת כל דם הפר ישפוך', together with the layout: the כהן meets the western side first when he exits the היכל.

steps.title: The משנה's rule: leftover blood of outer offerings goes on the southern base
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: leftover blood from the outer altar's sprinklings is poured on the southern יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the leftover blood of the outer altar he would pour on the southern base.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה. This line covers offerings whose blood is placed on the outer altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These offerings are different from the inner ones in step 22. Their blood is put on the outer altar itself. The משנה says their leftover blood goes on the southern side, so the גמרא will look for a source.

phrases.english: And (the leftover blood) of the outer altar
he would pour on the southern base.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן הָיָה שׁוֹפֵךְ עַל יְסוֹד דְּרוֹמִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the inner offerings to the outer offerings, which have a different side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover blood from sprinklings on the outer altar is poured on the southern יסוד.

steps.title: A ברייתא: 'the base of the altar' means the southern base
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק's words 'יסוד המזבח' (said about outer offerings) as meaning the southern base.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our Rabbis taught: 'The base of the altar' — this is the southern base.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support the משנה's southern rule. The ברייתא states its claim first and proves it in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: About an individual's חטאת, the פסוק (ויקרא ד:ל) says only to pour at 'the base of the altar', without naming a side. The ברייתא says this means the southern side. Its proof is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The base of the altar': the phrase in the פסוק

phrases.english: Our Rabbis taught:
'The base of the altar' — this is the southern base.
phrases.notes: ויקרא ד:ל, said about the חטאת of an individual.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to back up the משנה's southern rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'יסוד המזבח' in the פסוק about outer offerings refers to the southern base.

steps.title: Why not the western base?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks itself: maybe it means the western base, the same as for inner offerings?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say the southern base? Or perhaps it means only the western base?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question to test its own claim. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the inner offerings use the western base. So a reader could think 'the base' always means west. The ברייתא raises this possibility so it can rule it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is only...: a standard ברייתא way of testing a reading

phrases.english: Do you say the southern base?
Or perhaps it is only the western base?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר יְסוֹד דְּרוֹמִית, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא יְסוֹד מַעֲרָבִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the ברייתא's claim from step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why read 'the base' as south rather than west?

steps.title: Each time, he pours at the nearest side
steps.stepSummary: Coming down the כבש is compared to coming out of the היכל. Both times he pours at the closest side: west after the היכל, south after the כבש.
steps.simpleTranslation: You said: let his coming down from the ramp be learned from his going out from the היכל. When he goes out from the היכל, he pours at the side closest to him, which is the western base. So too, when he comes down from the ramp, he pours at the side closest to him, which is the southern base.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. The rule is 'pour at the nearest side', and that nearest side changes depending on where he is coming from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison does not copy the direction 'west'. It copies the principle of 'closest to him'. The כבש (ramp) is on the south side of the altar. So when the כהן comes down after sprinkling, the southern base is the nearest one.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp of the altar, on its south side
The Sanctuary building, to the west of the altar
At the side closest to him

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the comparison makes both offerings use the same side. What is learned is 'nearest side', and that is why the answers differ: west for one, south for the other.
steps.whatToRemember: For both kinds of offerings, the leftover blood goes at the nearest base. For the inner offerings that is west (coming out of the היכל). For the outer offerings that is south (coming down the כבש).

phrases.english: You said (i.e., the answer is):
Let his coming down from the ramp be learned
from his going out from the היכל.

phrases.aramaic: מָה יְצִיאָתוֹ מִן הַהֵיכָל בְּסָמוּךְ לוֹ,
phrases.english: Just as on going out from the היכל, (he pours) at the side closest to him,
and which is that? It is the western base,

phrases.aramaic: אַף יְרִידָתוֹ מִן הַכֶּבֶשׁ, בְּסָמוּךְ לוֹ,
phrases.english: so too on coming down from the ramp, (he pours) at the side closest to him,
and which is that? It is the southern base.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתָּ: יִלְמַד יְרִידָתוֹ מִן הַכֶּבֶשׁ לִיצִיאָתוֹ מִן הַהֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26 by comparing to the case of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both cases follow 'nearest side'. Coming down the כבש, the nearest side is the south.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי disagree
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי ישמעאל says both kinds of leftover blood go on the western base. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says both go on the southern base.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי ישמעאל says: both this and that go on the western base. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says: both this and that go on the southern base.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא with two opinions that disagree with the split rule we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'This and that' means the leftover blood of the inner offerings and of the outer offerings. Each תנא puts both on one side: רבי ישמעאל on the west, רבי שמעון בן יוחאי on the south. Neither one splits them the way the משנה does.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that: both the inner and the outer leftover blood

phrases.english: It was taught: רבי ישמעאל says:
Both this and that (go on) the western base.
רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says:
Both this and that (go on) the southern base.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: זֶה וָזֶה יְסוֹד מַעֲרָבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents two opinions that differ from the משנה's split (west for inner, south for outer).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל: all leftover blood goes west. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: all leftover blood goes south.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's reasoning is clear: learn the unclear from the clear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that רבי ישמעאל's view makes sense: the unspecified case (outer offerings) is learned from the explicit one (inner offerings, west). This sets up a question on רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, רבי ישמעאל holds: let the unclear be learned from the clear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי ישמעאל's view as a setup. The word בשלמא signals that the next move will be to ask what the reasoning of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the inner offerings, the Torah's description makes the western side clear, as step 23 showed. For the outer offerings, the פסוק just says 'the base'. רבי ישמעאל copies the clear case into the unclear one, so both go west. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי has no obvious reason yet, and that is what the גמרא is about to challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted: we understand this side (setting up a 'but what about the other?')

phrases.english: Granted, רבי ישמעאל holds:
Let the unclear be learned from the explicit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to analyze the dispute of step 28, beginning with the opinion that is easy to understand.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי that both go south (the question itself is completed next).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ישמעאל has a clear reason (ילמד סתום ממפורש). The implied challenge: what source lets רבי שמעון בן יוחאי send even the inner offerings' blood south, against the clear case?

steps.title: What is the reasoning of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי?
steps.stepSummary: Having granted that רבי ישמעאל's view makes sense, the גמרא now asks what reasoning supports רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's 'southern base for both' view.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it set up in the last step. It asks: why would רבי שמעון בן יוחאי say that even the leftover blood from the inner offerings goes on the southern base?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 showed that רבי ישמעאל has a clear source: learn the unclear case (outer offerings) from the clear case (inner offerings, which go on the west). רבי שמעון בן יוחאי seems to go the other way, and even moves the inner offerings to the south. That needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: But, however. Here it means: that view is fine, but what about the other one?

phrases.english: But Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai,
what is his reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי, מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that step 29 set up
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's view that both kinds of leftover blood go on the southern base
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Step 23 (and the comparison in step 27) linked the inner offerings to the western base, which the כהן reaches first on leaving the היכל. So what basis is there for putting the inner offerings' blood on the south?

steps.title: רב אשי: the entrance lines up with the south
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that רבי שמעון בן יוחאי holds the entrance of the היכל is positioned opposite the southern part of the מזבח, so the south is the closest side even when the כהן גדול comes out of the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: He holds that the entrance stands in the south.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי pictures the layout of the עזרה differently: when the כהן גדול walks out of the היכל, the southern side of the מזבח is the part right in front of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees with the rule from step 27: pour at the side closest to where you just were. The argument is only about the map. If the מזבח sits toward the north of the courtyard, then the doorway of the היכל lines up with the מזבח's southern half, so the southern base is closest for inner offerings too.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, he is of the opinion
Stands in the south (lines up with the southern side)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי is NOT rejecting the 'closest side' logic from step 27. He agrees with it. He only disagrees about where the doorway is positioned relative to the מזבח.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
He holds that the entrance stands in the south.
phrases.notes: The מזבח is shifted to the north, so the היכל's doorway faces its southern part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different picture of the facts (the layout of the עזרה), not a different rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי seemed to have no reason to move the inner offerings' blood off the western base
steps.terutzMaskana: He uses the same 'closest side' rule, but because the entrance lines up with the south, the southern base is closest for both

steps.title: A second version: רבי ישמעאל's school also says south
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught, in line with the school of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, that both kinds of blood go on the southern base. A memory aid is given: the men pulled the man.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught, like the school of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: Both this and that go on the southern base. And your memory aid: The men pulled the man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching showing that רבי ישמעאל's school ended up ruling 'southern base' for both, just like רבי שמעון בן יוחאי. Then it gives a short phrase to help you remember who agreed with whom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רבי ישמעאל no longer holds 'western base'; he came around to the southern view. The memory aid 'the men pulled the man' means the many (the school of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי) won over the single person (רבי ישמעאל).

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of
This and that (the inner and outer offerings' blood)
The southern base of the מזבח
The men pulled the man (the many convinced the one)

steps.whyThisMatters: It suggests that the 'southern base' view may be the more widely accepted one, since even רבי ישמעאל's school taught it.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught
like the school of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
Both this and that go on the southern base.
And your memory aid:
The men pulled the man.
phrases.notes: The many students of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי drew רבי ישמעאל to their view.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בִּדְבֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רבי ישמעאל's opinion than the one in step 28
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this version, both inner and outer leftover blood go on the southern base, and רבי ישמעאל agrees
steps.whatToRemember: Main rule: pour leftover blood at the side closest to where you came from. The משנה splits the cases: west for inner offerings, south for outer offerings. In the first ברייתא, רבי ישמעאל says west for both, learning the unclear case from the clear one (ילמד סתום ממפורש). רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says south for both, because the doorway lines up with the south. In a second version, רבי ישמעאל's school also says south for both.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the blood mixes in the canal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: both kinds of leftover blood mix in the אמה (the canal) and flow out.
steps.simpleTranslation: These and those mix in the canal and flow out, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. This is a setup line: it brings the line about the blood flowing out through the canal so the גמרא can discuss it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood from the inner offerings and the outer offerings ends up together in a canal under the מזבח. From there it flows out to the נחל קדרון, where it was sold to gardeners as fertilizer. The 'etc.' signals that the rest of that משנה line, about selling it and about מעילה, is the topic now.

keyTerms.meaning: These and those (both kinds of blood)
The canal (a water channel in the עזרה)

phrases.english: These and those mix in the canal
and flow out, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the base question to the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both kinds of leftover blood mix in the canal and flow out of the עזרה

steps.title: A ברייתא: is there מעילה with the blood?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a מחלוקת. רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון say one who uses the blood commits מעילה. The חכמים say there is no מעילה with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One commits מעילה with the blood, these are the words of רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון. And the חכמים say: One does not commit מעילה with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with an argument about whether this blood still counts as holy property. If it does, using it without paying the הקדש is the sin of מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון hold that the blood stays הקדש even after it flows out, so taking it without redeeming it is מעילה. The חכמים hold that once the blood has done its job on the מזבח, there is no מעילה with it. This sets up the next discussion about the reasons for each side.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood (here, the leftover blood of offerings)

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה says the blood is sold to gardeners. That does not settle this argument. The question is whether someone who takes it WITHOUT paying commits מעילה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One commits misuse of holy property with the blood —
these are the words of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon.
And the Sages say:
One does not commit misuse with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that explains the מעילה part of the משנה line just quoted
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון: there is מעילה with the leftover blood. חכמים: there is no מעילה with it.
